sentences.text: The important facts of the case are that on 14.09.2018 at about 08:10 p.m. the deceased Rajbali Ram sustained fatal injuries on account of a motor vehicular accident occurred at Red Light, Shani Mandir, near Hasanpur Depot, Delhi.
In connection with the accident, the case FIR no.0302/2018 under sections 279/337 was registered at PS Madhu Vihar.

During the investigation, the eyewitness Vikas Dass revealed that on the aforesaid date, time and place, while the deceased was crossing the road, a Chhota Hathi vehicle bearing no. DL1L-Y4326 (in short 'offending vehicle'), being driven by its driver at a fast speed hit him, as a result of which, he sustained serious injuries.
The deceased was taken to hospital, where he died during treatment and accordingly, section 304-A IPC was added in the case.

3. During the investigation, it was found that the offending vehicle was being driven at high speed and in rash and negligent manner by respondent no. 1, which was owned by respondent no. 2 and i n s u r e d ______________________________________________________________________ with respondent no. 3.
The DAR has been treated as claim petition under section 166(4) of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 for a grant of compensation to the claimants/ legal heirs of the deceased.
4. In response to the notice of claim petition, all the three respondents appeared and filed their separate written-statements.

5. Respondent no. 1 and 2 in their respective written-statement denied to have caused the alleged accident involving the offending vehicle and submitted that they have been falsely implicated in this case by the police.

They also stated that at the time of the accident, the offending vehicle was duly insured with respondent no. 3 Tata AIG General Insurance Co. Ltd. and therefore, liability if any,
could be fastened upon the insurance company.

On this issue, PW2 Vikas Das testified that on 14.09.2018 at about 08:15 p.m., he was dropped by his friend at Red Light, Hasanpur after his work and while he was crossing the said Red Light, he saw that the deceased was crossing the Red Light before Bus Stop and, in the meantime, a vehicle bearing no. DL-1LY-4326, being driven rashly and negligently, came and hit the deceased who was crossing the road on foot, as a result of which he fell down on the road and started bleeding profusely.
PW2 stated that thereafter, driver stopped the offending vehicle and took the deceased to hospital.
PW2 stated that he informed the police at 100 number regarding the accident.
The e y e w i t n e s s c a t e g o r i c a l l y s t a t e d t h a t t h e a c c i d e n t t o o k p l a c e d u e ____________________________________________________________________
__ to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle because had the driver been cautious enough, this accident could have been averted.
12. PW2 was cross-examined at length by learned counsel for the insurance company.

13. It may be noted that during cross-examination, PW2 was put a suggestion inter-alia that a bus dashed/ hit some unknown person (deceased) to which he promptly denied and voluntarily stated that it was Chhota Hathi and made it clear that it was being driven at the speed of 70-80 kmph.
PW2 replied that he made a call at 100 number from his mobile number i.e. 85274-00871 disclosing the number of offending vehicle.

Further, made it clear that he saw the driver at the time of the accident,
who took the deceased to the hospital and he identified the driver in MACT Cell on 06.10.2018.
14.

Having gone through the entire deposition of the eyewitness PW2, who has also been cited as an eyewitness in the charge-sheet and is an independent witness, this Tribunal finds nothing which may demolish or impeach his testimony on the aspect of a rash and negligent act of respondent no. 1 while driving the offending vehicle.
Besides, nothing else is available on record which may suggest any falsity or untruth in the oral testimony of eye-witness.
15. Further, there is no challenge from the respondent no. 1/ driver of the offending vehicle to the version of the petitioners.

The respondent no. 1 was the best witness, who could have stepped into t h e  
w i t n e s s ______________________________________________________________________ box to challenge the testimony of the eyewitness (PW2) regarding the above accident and its manner but he preferred not to enter into the witness box during the course of inquiry.

Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by him in view of the law laid down in case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. v. Kamlesh, 2009(3) AD (Delhi) 310.
16.

sentences.text: It is not disputed that the respondent no. 1 was charge-sheeted in the criminal case for the offences under Sections 279/337/304-A IPC 3/181 of Motor Vehicle Act.

The Site Plan of the place of accident, Seizure Memo and mechanical inspection report of the offending vehicle, which are part of the DAR also supports the occurrence of the accident as per version of the eyewitness.
Thus, it may be discernible that respondent no. 1 was negligent in driving the offending vehicle at the time of the accident.

17. The copy of MLC prepared at Max Hospital, Delhi, which is part of the DAR Ex.PW1/6 (colly)
shows that the injured Rajbali Ram was brought to the hospital immediately after the accident and this MLC clearly reflects the alleged history of RTA (Road Traffic Accident).

_______________ Further, it is evident that the postmortem of the deceased was got conducted at LBS Hospital, Delhi and as per postmortem report, the death of deceased Rajbali Ram was caused by shock due to antemortem cerebral damage consequent upon the blunt force impact on the head and all the injuries were antemortem in nature, fresh in duration and could be possible to cause by in manner as alleged.
18. Besides above, it is settled proposition of law that in an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.

However,
the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of the preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012,
Bimla Devi & Others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530,
Parmeshwari v. Amirchand & Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Co.
Ltd. & Ors. 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303.
19.

sentences.text: Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to be just and reasonable.
It has to be borne in mind that the compensation is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be a pittance.

22. In Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121, the relevant guidelines were laid down for death cases, which have been reiterated by the Constitution Bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court in a case titled as National Insurance Company vs.
Pranay Sethi & Ors. (AIR 2017 SC 5157), decided on 31.10.2017, laying down the general principles for computation of compensation in death cases.

The relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced here as under:
"18.
It will also be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.

19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income, a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balance which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.

Dar - Mahendra Ram vs Kuldeep Singh on 7 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37856493/
6 Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)

entities.text: Dar - Mahendra Ram vs Kuldeep Singh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.

The m u l t i p l i e r s h o u l d b e c h o s e n f r o m t h e s a i d t a b l e w i t h ______________________________________________________________________ reference to the age of the deceased.

Step-3 (Actual Calculation) The annual contribution to the family (multiplicand)
when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.
Thereafter, a conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000/- to Rs.10,000/- may be added as loss of estates.
Where the deceased is survived by his widow, another conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000 to Rs.10,000 should be added under the head of loss of consortium.
But no amount is to be awarded under the head of pain, suffering or hardship caused to the legal heirs of the deceased.
The funeral expenses, cost of transportation of the body (if incurred) and the cost of any medical treatment of the deceased before death (if incurred) should also be added."

Therefore, in view of the aforesaid judgment, it is essential to take into consideration the following parameters:
PECUNIARY DAMAGE Age of deceased 23.
Aadhaar Card of the deceased, which has been proved on record as Ex.PW1/1 reflects his year of birth as 1962.
Accordingly, the age of deceased comes to 56 years on the date of accident i.e. on 14.09.2018.
Assessment of Income of deceased 24.

PW1 Mahendra Ram deposed that is deceased father was working as a Guard and apart from that, he was also doing the work of Mason and was earning a sum of R s . 2 0 , 0 0 0 / - p e r m o n t h . Further, he did not place on record any documentary evidence in support of his claim regarding occupation and income of the deceased nor he produced any document to show education of the deceased.

It may be noted that on page 16 of the DAR the occupation of the deceased has been stated to be that of the security guard only and monthly income of Rs.12,000/-
per month.

But in the DAR, it has not been disclosed that if the deceased was working as a security guard where exactly the deceased was working, who was the employer,
etc.

Without any semblance of a tangible fact, any assertions made with respect to the occupation/job of the deceased, his monthly income whether by PW1 in his deposition or by the investigating officer in the DAR cannot be assumed even on the balance of probability to have been proved.
26. On record the best piece of evidence is the Aadhaar Card.
The Aadhaar Card of all the claimants and that of the deceased show their residential address of Bihar.

27. In these circumstances, in the absence of any documentary evidence with respect to income and education of the deceased, his income has to be assessed at par with minimum wages of an unskilled category worker of Bihar on the date of accident (14.09.2018), which were Rs.254/- per day.

Thus, the income of the deceased is a s s e s s e d  
t o  
b e ______________________________________________________________________ Rs.6,604/- (254x26) per month.
Application of Multiplier 28.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
The judgment titled as Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121 is relevant to consider the multiplier.

In Para 21 of the judgment, the guidelines for the multiplier were laid down in accordance with age are as under:
MULTIPLIER AGE GROUP OF DECEASED M-18 Age group between 15 to 20 & 21 to 25 years) M-17 Age group between 26 to 30 yrs M-16 Age group between 31 to 35 yrs M-15 Age group between 36 to 40 yrs M-14 Age group between 41 to 45 yrs M-13 Age group between 46 to 50 yrs M-11 Age group between 51 to 55 yrs M-9 Age group between 56 to 60 yrs M-7 Age group between 61 to 65 yrs M-5 Age group between 66 and above The deceased was 56 years of age at the time of the accident.
Accordingly
, in view of the above said judgment, a multiplier of 9, applicable to the age group of 56-60 years has to be applied in this case to determine the compensation.
This issue was considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pranay Sethi & Others (Supra).

Relevant parts of the judgment are reproduced here as under:

sentences.text: The addition should be 30%, if the age of the deceased was between 40 to 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years, the addition should be 15%.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.
(iv) In case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.
An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component.
The deceased can be considered a self-employed.
In view of the aforementioned judgment, an addition of 10% of the income of the deceased, who belonged to the age group of 50-60 years has to be considered towards future prospects.
Deduction Towards Personal Living Expenses 30.
After choosing the age, multiplier and income of the deceased, necessary deductions have to be made out of the income of the deceased towards his personal expenses.

Hence, half of the income of the deceased is to be deducted towards his personal living expenses.

33. The accident in this case occurred on 14.09.2018.

Therefore, a compensation of Rs.40,000/-,
Rs.15,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is required to be granted.

Further, in view of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case titled as United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Now, the question arises as to which of the respondents is liable to pay the compensation amount.

37. Admittedly, the insurance company has contractual and statutory liability to indemnify the insured, however, in this case, learned counsel for insurance company contended that respondent Dar - Mahendra Ram vs Kuldeep Singh on 7 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37856493/

Learned counsel for the insurance company stated that R3W1 Ms. Asmita Singh, Manager (Legal) of the insurance company has proved on record the copy o f  
i n s u r a n c e ______________________________________________________________________ policy as Ex.R3W1/1, copy of notice under order 12 rule 8 CPC, dated 20.12.2022 sent to the registered owner to produce the driving license of the driver, as Ex.R3W1/2, original postal receipts dated 22.12.2022 as Ex.R3W1/3 and copy of tracking reports as Ex.R3W1/4 and thus, there is a clear violation of the Drivers Clause of the insurance policy (Ex.R3W1/1) and hence, insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation in this case.

38. It is noteworthy that respondent nos. 1 and 2 did not adduce any evidence to disprove the version of R3W1 and thus, the violation of the Driver's Clause stands established on record and therefore, insurance company is entitled to get recovery rights.

Hence, this Tribunal is of the view that in order to serve the ends of justice in the facts and circumstances of this case, respondent no.
3/ insurance company should be directed to pay the compensation and thereafter, it should recover the same from the owner and driver.

Accordingly, it is held that respondent no. 3/ insurance company shall deposit the awarded amount with this Tribunal and thereafter, it shall be entitled to get the paid amount recovered from the respondent no. 1 and 2, jointly or severally in accordance with law.

the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of the preponderance of probabilities.

19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income, a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balance which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
Accordingly, the age of deceased comes to 56 years on the date of accident i.e. on 14.09.2018.

An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
